messages.content: I need to start planning Atlanta for October 15 through 18. The opening reception is Wednesday at 6:00 p.m., appointments run all day Thursday and Friday, and the publishers' roundtable ends at 12:30 Saturday. I will be traveling alone from Denver and need three hotel nights near the conference complex.
I can compare the trip as complete flight-and-hotel combinations. Which Atlanta conference complex is it, and do you have a target airfare or hotel budget?

It is at the Georgia World Congress Center. Keep the hotel under $900 total if possible, including taxes. I am less concerned about finding the cheapest flight than about having enough time to get to the reception without turning Wednesday into a very early morning.

For a 6:00 p.m. reception at the GWCC, I would plan to reach the hotel by about 4:30. That leaves time for check-in, a short reset, and the walk to the venue. From an ATL gate, allow roughly 60 to 80 minutes for the Plane Train, MARTA to downtown, and the final walk; a taxi or rideshare can take 25 to 45 minutes in ordinary traffic but can run longer during the afternoon. A flight landing by 3:00 p.m. is workable, while one landing near 4:00 would be fragile. Do you want me to focus on nonstops?
Yes, compare nonstops. I can leave home at a reasonable morning hour, just not at dawn. What Wednesday choices does that produce?

Three representative nonstop schedules fit the day: a 9:35 a.m. Denver departure arriving Atlanta at 2:35 p.m.; an 11:05 a.m. departure arriving at 4:02 p.m.; and a 12:40 p.m. departure arriving at 5:35 p.m. The first gives about 3 hours 25 minutes before the reception and should put you downtown around 3:45 to 4:05. The 11:05 flight leaves only about two hours after landing and could get you to the hotel around 5:15 on a smooth trip. The last flight cannot support the reception. Current round-trip estimates, paired with reasonable Saturday returns, are $438, $401, and $376 respectively.
Set aside the last one. Is the 11:05 genuinely possible, or are we pretending nothing will go wrong?

It is possible but not a sound conference plan. A 4:02 scheduled arrival can become a 4:15 gate arrival, and a checked bag or traffic delay could consume the remaining margin. Even with MARTA, you might reach the hotel only 30 to 40 minutes before the reception. The 9:35 departure is the better choice: it is not exceptionally early from Denver and preserves roughly 75 to 100 minutes of disruption tolerance.
Use the 9:35 outbound in the combinations. Now compare hotels where I can walk to the GWCC. I do not need a resort; I need a straightforward room and an easy route back after appointments.

The strongest three-night candidates are the Omni Atlanta at Centennial Park, about a 4-minute walk from the main GWCC entrances, at an estimated $846 including taxes; the Glenn Hotel, about 9 minutes on foot, at approximately $782 total; and the Hilton Garden Inn Atlanta Downtown, about a 10-minute walk, at approximately $735 total. The Omni minimizes daily transit and is directly useful if your appointments are spread across the complex. The Glenn is the middle-cost option but has a slightly less direct route. The Hilton Garden Inn saves about $111 versus the Omni while remaining comfortably walkable.
Does the Omni figure include the destination fee and taxes? Conference hotel quotes have surprised me before.

The $846 estimate includes the displayed room charge, estimated occupancy and sales taxes, and the currently disclosed nightly destination charge. It does not include parking or incidentals. Because fee treatment can change by rate, the booking screen should still be checked for a final all-in total before purchase. The comparable $782 and $735 figures also include estimated taxes and disclosed mandatory fees.
Please put the flight and hotels together. Include how I would get from the airport and what time I could realistically be in the room.

Combination one is the 9:35 a.m. nonstop, arriving 2:35 p.m., plus the Omni at $846 for three nights. Using MARTA, take the airport train to Five Points and transfer toward GWCC/CNN Center; including station movement and the hotel walk, expect to arrive around 3:45 to 4:05. A rideshare could reach the Omni around 3:25 to 3:55, depending on pickup and traffic. Combination two uses the same flight and the Glenn at $782. MARTA to Five Points followed by an approximately 8-minute walk should put you there around 3:40 to 4:00. Combination three pairs the flight with the Hilton Garden Inn at $735; MARTA via Peachtree Center or the Centennial Park area should yield roughly a 3:50 to 4:10 hotel arrival. All three leave time before 6:00, but the Omni has the easiest conference access.
What does Saturday look like? I cannot leave the roundtable before 12:30, and I will have luggage.

Plan to store your bag with the hotel after checkout and retrieve it immediately after the roundtable. From the GWCC area, a conservative sequence is 12:30 adjournment, 12:45 hotel arrival, 1:00 departure for ATL, and 1:45 to 2:15 airport arrival. That makes a nonstop at 3:40 p.m. the earliest comfortable return. There is also a 5:25 p.m. nonstop that creates much more margin. A 2:25 p.m. flight is technically reachable only if everything is immediate and traffic is light, so I would exclude it.
Compare the 3:40 and 5:25 returns. I would rather not spend the whole afternoon at the airport, but I also cannot have the roundtable clock become a problem.

The 3:40 return gives you about 85 to 115 minutes at ATL under the conservative transfer estimate. That is adequate if the session ends on time, your bag is ready, and there is no major road or rail disruption, but it leaves little room for a conversation running past 12:30. Its round-trip pairing with the 9:35 outbound is about $438. The 5:25 return raises the estimated airfare to $467 and gives you roughly 3 hours 10 minutes to 3 hours 40 minutes at the airport. More importantly, it absorbs a delayed adjournment, luggage retrieval, and ordinary Saturday congestion.
Could I have lunch downtown and still take the 5:25?

Yes, if lunch stays near the hotel or Centennial Park. A workable plan is to retrieve your bag by 12:50, eat from about 1:00 to 1:45, and leave downtown no later than 2:15. That should put you at ATL around 3:00 to 3:30, leaving nearly two hours before departure at the better end of the range and at least about 90 minutes if traffic is slow. Keep the luggage with the hotel during lunch rather than carrying it back to the GWCC.
Then compare only two final packages: Omni with the later return and Hilton Garden Inn with the earlier return. Include the combined totals and tell me which tradeoff is more sensible.

Package A is the 9:35 a.m. Wednesday nonstop, the 5:25 p.m. Saturday nonstop, and three nights at the Omni. Estimated airfare is $467 and lodging is $846, for a combined $1,313 before airport transfers and meals. It gives the shortest conference walk, a realistic Wednesday arrival around 3:45 to 4:05 by MARTA, and enough Saturday margin for lunch. Package B is the same outbound, the 3:40 p.m. return, and the Hilton Garden Inn. Estimated airfare is $438 and lodging is $735, totaling $1,173 before transfers and meals. It saves $140, but adds about six minutes to each conference walk and makes Saturday dependent on a prompt 12:30 finish and quick bag retrieval.
The $140 difference is acceptable. Choose the package that does not make Saturday feel like a race, but do not book it yet. Give me the final schedule and the items that need live verification.

Choose Package A: depart Denver Wednesday, October 15 at 9:35 a.m., arrive Atlanta at 2:35 p.m.; stay three nights at the Omni Atlanta at Centennial Park; and return Saturday, October 18 on the 5:25 p.m. nonstop. The working total is $1,313: $467 airfare plus $846 lodging, before local transportation and meals. Wednesday, MARTA should put you at the hotel around 3:45 to 4:05, leaving nearly two hours before the reception. Saturday, store your luggage after checkout, attend the roundtable through 12:30, retrieve the bag, have a nearby lunch, and leave downtown by 2:15 for ATL. Before booking, verify the exact flight numbers and live fares, nonstop status, baggage terms, and any schedule changes; confirm the hotel rate covers October 15-18, the room type, cancellation deadline, taxes, and every mandatory destination fee; and check whether the conference uses the GWCC building closest to the Omni. Nothing has been booked.
